They obtain analytic expressions for asymptotic energy values and show that models with sufficiently separated interaction orders (s>3) have a fully continuous phase reaching the algorithmic energy lower bound, while mixed models with only high-order interactions (p≥3) stay strictly above it. Numerical integration confirms the predicted two-step and mixed discrete-continuous aging states.
AI.motivation: Understanding the out-of-equilibrium aging dynamics of glassy systems is a fundamental challenge. Mixed spherical spin glasses serve as canonical models where the Cugliandolo-Kurchan equations can be solved asymptotically, allowing a rigorous classification of aging states based on effective temperatures and energy relaxation — insights that reveal universal structure in complex relaxation phenomena.
AI.method: The authors solve the asymptotic form of the Cugliandolo-Kurchan dynamical equations for mixed spherical (p+s)-spin glasses quenched from random initial configurations to zero temperature. They analyze the structure of the solutions to classify aging states by the number of effective temperatures (one, two, or continuous many), including mixed discrete-continuous hierarchies. Analytic expressions for asymptotic energies are derived, and results are verified via numerical integration of the dynamical equations.
AI.result: The aging phase diagram exhibits transitions between phases with one, two, and continuously many effective temperatures, including coexisting discrete and continuous hierarchical phases. For models with pairwise and higher-order interactions where s>3, a fully continuous phase exists where relaxation reaches the algorithmic energy lower bound. In contrast, mixed models with only high-order interactions (p≥3) remain strictly above this bound. Numerical integration confirms the predicted two-step and mixed discrete-continuous aging behavior.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a complete analytical characterization of zero-temperature aging dynamics in mixed spherical spin glasses, revealing a rich phase structure of effective temperatures and establishing precise conditions (s>3) under which gradient descent reaches algorithmic energy optimality. This deepens our understanding of dynamical transitions in glassy systems and the nature of hierarchical aging.

title: On Transmission Function Amplitude and Phase Recovery in Multislice Electron Ptychography
summary: {Multislice electron ptychography commonly accounts for inelastic scattering by including an absorptive object potential in the reconstruction forward model that attenuates the elastic signal. However, it remains unclear how the reconstruction is quantitatively impacted by thermal scattering. Here, we use the quantum excitation of phonons (QEP) formalism, which explicitly separates elastic and inelastic (thermal diffuse) scattering within a single multislice propagation, to simulate four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D STEM) datasets of PbTiO$_3$ and SrTiO$_3$ and reconstruct their phase and amplitude. We find that reconstructions of the QEP total and elastic-only datasets are nearly indistinguishable across sample thicknesses from 11 to 40 nm and across atomic species, demonstrating that the reconstruction is largely insensitive to incoherent thermal diffuse scattering within the collected angular range. Reconstructions from multislice phase-only simulations further confirm that appreciable amplitude does not arise from multiple elastic scattering, but instead reflects attenuation of the coherent elastic signal due to thermal scattering. Further comparison of the QEP elastic-only reconstruction with absorptive multislice simulations reveals substantial amplitude contrast deviations for heavy Pb columns (up to 17\%), arising from the approximations used to evaluate the absorptive potential for the 4D STEM simulation. These results thus indicate that reconstruction phase and amplitude accuracy are not significantly limited by the absorptive potential forward model, even in the presence of thermal diffuse scattering.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how thermal diffuse scattering affects multislice electron ptychography reconstructions by comparing QEP simulations (which explicitly separate elastic and inelastic scattering) with standard absorptive potential forward models for PbTiO3 and SrTiO3 across thicknesses of 11-40 nm. Reconstructions from QEP total and elastic-only datasets are nearly indistinguishable, indicating insensitivity to incoherent thermal scattering within the collected angular range, though heavy Pb columns show amplitude deviations up to 17% due to approximations in the absorptive potential. The results show reconstruction accuracy is not significantly limited by the absorptive potential forward model.
AI.motivation: To determine how quantitatively thermal scattering impacts multislice electron ptychography reconstructions, specifically whether the commonly used absorptive object potential forward model (which attenuates elastic signal to account for inelastic scattering) provides accurate phase and amplitude reconstructions in the presence of thermal diffuse scattering.
AI.method: Using the quantum excitation of phonons (QEP) formalism, which explicitly separates elastic and inelastic (thermal diffuse) scattering within a single multislice propagation, the authors simulate 4D STEM datasets of PbTiO3 and SrTiO3 and reconstruct their phase and amplitude. They compare reconstructions from QEP total and elastic-only datasets, contrast them with multislice phase-only simulations, and compare QEP elastic-only reconstructions with absorptive multislice simulations.
AI.result: Reconstructions from QEP total and elastic-only datasets are nearly indistinguishable across thicknesses from 11 to 40 nm and across atomic species. Multislice phase-only simulations confirm that amplitude in reconstructions reflects attenuation of coherent elastic signal due to thermal scattering rather than multiple elastic scattering. Heavy Pb columns show substantial amplitude contrast deviations (up to 17%) when comparing QEP elastic-only reconstructions with absorptive multislice simulations.
AI.conclusion: Reconstruction phase and amplitude accuracy are not significantly limited by the absorptive potential forward model, even in the presence of thermal diffuse scattering, although the approximations used to evaluate the absorptive potential for heavy elements can introduce notable amplitude deviations.

title: Orbital-Optimized Quasi-Variational Distinguishable Cluster Doubles Method
summary: We present the orbital-optimized quasi-variational distinguishable cluster doubles (OQVDCD) method, obtained by applying the distinguishable cluster (DC) approximation to orbital-optimized quasi-variational coupled cluster doubles (OQVCCD). The resulting method retains a Hermitian-like energy functional, is size-extensive, obeys the generalized Hellmann-Feynman theorem at a stationary point, is exact in the isolated two-electron and two-hole limits, and scales as O(o2v4), like coupled cluster singles and doubles (CCSD). For the tested closed-shell reaction energies, it is shown that OQVDCD reduces the mean absolute deviation relative to OQVCCD from 1.20 to 0.81 kcal/mol, bringing the errors close to distinguishable cluster singles and doubles (DCSD). In the strongly correlated examples considered here, OQVDCD shifts the OQVCCD energies toward the benchmark, although the convergence remains somewhat less robust than for DCSD.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the orbital-optimized quasi-variational distinguishable cluster doubles (OQVDCD) method, combining the distinguishable cluster approximation with quasi-variational coupled cluster doubles. It retains favorable properties like size-extensivity and Hellmann-Feynman compliance while improving accuracy over OQVCCD, achieving errors close to DCSD at the same O(o2v4) scaling.
AI.motivation: To improve the accuracy of orbital-optimized quasi-variational coupled cluster doubles (OQVCCD) by applying the distinguishable cluster (DC) approximation, which is known to yield better accuracy in strongly correlated and reaction energy contexts, while maintaining the desirable theoretical properties and computational scaling of the parent method.
AI.method: OQVDCD is derived by applying the distinguishable cluster approximation to the OQVCCD method. The paper evaluates its theoretical properties (Hermitian-like energy functional, size-extensivity, generalized Hellmann-Feynman theorem, two-electron/two-hole exactness) and its computational scaling of O(o2v4), analogous to CCSD.
AI.result: For tested closed-shell reaction energies, OQVDCD reduces the mean absolute deviation relative to OQVCCD from 1.20 to 0.81 kcal/mol, bringing errors close to DCSD. In strongly correlated examples, OQVDCD shifts OQVCCD energies toward the benchmark, though its convergence is somewhat less robust than DCSD.
AI.conclusion: OQVDCD is a promising method that improves upon OQVCCD accuracy—particularly for reaction energies and strongly correlated systems—approaching DCSD-quality results while retaining the same computational scaling, albeit with slightly less robust convergence in strongly correlated regimes.

title: Towards Ultra Scalability of Non-Volatile Magnetic Tunnel Junctions with a 3D Storage Layer
summary: The perpendicular Spin Transfer Torque Magnetic Random Access Memory is one of the most promising emerging non-volatile memory technologies, based on ultra-thin magnetic tunnel junctions. However, as these devices are limited by their thermal stability factor at technological nodes smaller than 20 nm, their scalability is compromised. A possible solution to this limitation relies on taking advantage of the shape anisotropy, by increasing substantially the thickness of the storage layer. Thanks to the combination of a vertical aspect-ratio and enhanced volume, high thermal stability can be maintained at sub-10 nm nodes. Here, we present the technological advancements and understanding of the magnetisation reversal that led to faster switching speeds at reduced switching voltage, providing a viable approach for dense arrays of ultra-small magnetic tunnel junctions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a solution to the thermal stability scaling limitation of perpendicular Spin Transfer Torque Magnetic Random Access Memory (STT-MRAM) at sub-10 nm nodes by increasing the thickness of the storage layer to exploit shape anisotropy with a vertical aspect ratio, resulting in faster switching speeds at reduced switching voltages for ultra-small magnetic tunnel junctions.
AI.motivation: Perpendicular STT-MRAM is a promising non-volatile memory technology, but its thermal stability factor degrades at technological nodes smaller than 20 nm, compromising scalability. A solution is needed to maintain high thermal stability at sub-10 nm dimensions.
AI.method: The approach leverages shape anisotropy by substantially increasing the storage layer thickness, combining a vertical aspect-ratio with enhanced volume to maintain high thermal stability at sub-10 nm nodes. The technological advancements and understanding of magnetization reversal are presented to optimize switching performance.
AI.result: The method provides a viable approach for dense arrays of ultra-small magnetic tunnel junctions, achieving faster switching speeds at reduced switching voltage.
AI.conclusion: Increasing the storage layer thickness to exploit shape anisotropy offers a viable path to maintain thermal stability and improve switching performance in perpendicular STT-MRAM at sub-10 nm technology nodes.

title: Superconducting ground state study of Cr-based equiatomic high-entropy alloy through $μ\text{SR}$
summary: High-entropy alloy superconductors, characterized by extreme chemical disorder and complex electronic environments, have attracted significant attention as model systems for exploring superconductivity in disordered materials. Here, we investigate a Cr-based equiatomic HEA, Cr-V-Ti-Nb-Ta, which contains a magnetic 3d element, providing an opportunity to examine the influence of magnetic elements on superconductivity in highly disordered systems. Despite expected magnetic pair-breaking, this alloy exhibits bulk type-II superconductivity with a transition temperature of $T_c = 2.33(3)$ K and a high upper critical field. Transverse-field $μ$SR measurements reveal an s-wave superconducting gap close to the BCS value, while zero-field $μ$SR suggests preserved time-reversal symmetry. These results establish Cr-V-Ti-Nb-Ta as a promising platform for exploring the interplay between disorder, magnetism and superconductivity in high entropy alloys.

AI.tldr: A Cr-based high-entropy alloy superconductor, Cr-V-Ti-Nb-Ta, exhibits bulk type-II superconductivity with Tc = 2.33 K despite containing a magnetic 3d element, showing an s-wave gap near the BCS value and preserved time-reversal symmetry.
AI.motivation: To examine how a magnetic 3d element influences superconductivity in highly disordered high-entropy alloy systems, where extreme chemical disorder and complex electronic environments coexist.
AI.method: Investigation of the equiatomic HEA Cr-V-Ti-Nb-Ta via transverse-field and zero-field muon spin rotation/relaxation (μSR) measurements, along with characterization of superconducting properties including transition temperature and upper critical field.
AI.result: The alloy shows bulk type-II superconductivity with Tc = 2.33(3) K and a high upper critical field. Transverse-field μSR reveals an s-wave superconducting gap close to the BCS value, and zero-field μSR indicates preserved time-reversal symmetry.
AI.conclusion: Cr-V-Ti-Nb-Ta is established as a promising platform for studying the interplay between disorder, magnetism, and superconductivity in high-entropy alloys, despite the expected magnetic pair-breaking from the Cr 3d element.

title: Berry-Curvature Effect in Anomalous Transport
summary: A theory of the Berry-phase effect in anomalous transport in ferromagnets driven by statistical forces such as the gradient of temperature or chemical potential has been developed by Di Xiao et al in Phys. Rev. Lett. 97, 026603 (2006) based on a field-dependent density of states generating an additional contribution to the current density. We present an alternative derivation of the Berry- phase effect in anomalous transport in altermagnets and noncentrosymmertric metals based on quasiclassic matrix kinetic equation. Along with anomalous Hall effect an anomalous heat flow and anomalous thermalelectric currents are also derived.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an alternative derivation of the Berry-phase effect in anomalous transport in altermagnets and noncentrosymmetric metals using a quasiclassical matrix kinetic equation, recovering results previously obtained by Di Xiao et al. via a field-dependent density of states approach, and additionally deriving anomalous heat flow and anomalous thermoelectric currents alongside the anomalous Hall effect.
AI.motivation: To provide an alternative theoretical framework for deriving the Berry-phase effect in anomalous transport, which was previously formulated by Di Xiao et al. using a field-dependent density of states, and to extend the treatment to anomalous transport in altermagnets and noncentrosymmetric metals including thermal and thermoelectric contributions.
AI.method: The authors employ a quasiclassical matrix kinetic equation approach to derive Berry-phase contributions to transport, as opposed to the field-dependent density of states method used by Di Xiao et al. This approach enables the derivation of anomalous Hall, anomalous heat flow, and anomalous thermoelectric currents in altermagnets and noncentrosymmetric metals.
AI.result: The quasiclassical matrix kinetic equation method provides an alternative derivation of the Berry-phase effect in anomalous transport, yielding the anomalous Hall effect along with additional anomalous heat flow and anomalous thermoelectric currents in altermagnets and noncentrosymmetric metals.
AI.conclusion: A quasiclassical matrix kinetic equation formulation can serve as an alternative and potentially more general framework for deriving Berry-phase-induced anomalous transport phenomena, including thermal and thermoelectric responses, in altermagnets and noncentrosymmetric metals.

title: Phase control of magnon-phonon coupling via magnetic field
summary: We study the phase of the coupling between magnons and surface acoustic wave (SAW) phonons in magnetic thin films. The coupling constant changes from a real to a complex number as the external magnetic field is reduced. Below a transition field, the imaginary coupling constant allows SAW phonons to couple to overdamped magnons whose resonance frequency is close to zero and far from the SAW resonance. The strength of the imaginary coupling constant and the magnitude of the transition field both scale with magnetic damping. We find the coupling produces a broad, pronounced minimum in the SAW transmittance spectrum near zero magnetic field in a Ni/Ru/Ni synthetic antiferromagnet with large magnetic damping. These results demonstrate that the phase of the complex magnon-phonon coupling constant can be tuned via magnetic field in strongly damped magnets, offering a platform to explore novel regimes of magnon-phonon interactions.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the phase of magnon-SAW phonon coupling in magnetic thin films, showing the coupling constant transitions from real to complex as the external magnetic field decreases. Below a transition field, imaginary coupling enables SAW phonons to interact with overdamped magnons near zero frequency, producing a broad transmittance minimum near zero field in a Ni/Ru/Ni synthetic antiferromagnet with high damping. The imaginary coupling strength and transition field both scale with magnetic damping.
AI.motivation: To understand and control the phase of the complex magnon-phonon coupling constant, which has not been previously explored, and to demonstrate that this phase can be tuned via magnetic field in strongly damped magnets.
AI.method: The study analyzes the coupling between magnons and SAW phonons in magnetic thin films, examining how the coupling constant evolves from real to complex with decreasing external magnetic field. The system is a Ni/Ru/Ni synthetic antiferromagnet with large magnetic damping, where the coupling behavior is characterized through transmittance spectrum measurements.
AI.result: Below a transition field, the imaginary coupling constant allows SAW phonons to couple to overdamped magnons with near-zero resonance frequency, far from the SAW resonance. The imaginary coupling strength and transition field magnitude both scale with magnetic damping. A broad, pronounced transmittance minimum near zero field was observed in the Ni/Ru/Ni synthetic antiferromagnet.
AI.conclusion: The phase of the complex magnon-phonon coupling constant can be tuned via magnetic field in strongly damped magnets, providing a platform to explore novel regimes of magnon-phonon interactions.

title: AutoMOOSE: Use Case and Logical Views of Agentic Phase-Field Simulation Software
summary: AutoMOOSE is an agentic software framework that converts a natural-language request into an executed, screened, and interpreted MOOSE phase-field simulation. Here, we deploy AutoMOOSE as a agentic software, complementing our prior work which focused on development of the agentic tool. We describe our software framework and architecture through Use Case and logical views of the 1+5 architectural-views model, covering its user roles, component structure, six-agent pipeline, physics plugin layer, Model Context Protocol interface, and screening/falsification/recovery loop. Our architecture separates physical falsification from automatic repair, so corrected simulations remain inspectable and must be re-admitted before acceptance. We focus on software design, extensibility, interoperability, and reuse of the AutoMoose framework for broad utilization in multiphysics materials design problems.

AI.tldr: This paper describes AutoMOOSE, an agentic software framework that converts natural-language requests into executed, screened, and interpreted MOOSE phase-field simulations, detailing its architecture through Use Case and logical views of the 1+5 architectural-views model.
AI.motivation: To complement prior work on the agentic tool's development by providing a detailed software architecture description, focusing on design, extensibility, interoperability, and reuse for broad multiphysics materials design applications.
AI.method: The paper presents AutoMOOSE's software framework and architecture using Use Case and logical views of the 1+5 architectural-views model, covering user roles, component structure, a six-agent pipeline, physics plugin layer, Model Context Protocol interface, and a screening/falsification/recovery loop. The architecture separates physical falsification from automatic repair so corrected simulations remain inspectable and must be re-admitted before acceptance.
AI.result: AutoMOOSE is deployed as an agentic software framework enabling natural-language-driven MOOSE phase-field simulations with a screening/falsification/recovery loop and an architecture that keeps physical falsification separate from automatic repair.
AI.conclusion: AutoMOOSE provides an extensible and interoperable agentic software framework for multiphysics materials design problems, with an architecture designed for broad reuse.

title: The Trachenko-Zaccone equation: nonlinear relaxation from glasses to complex systems
summary: The Trachenko-Zaccone equation provides a compact nonlinear dynamical framework for describing non-Debye relaxation in disordered condensed matter. Originally developed to rationalize stretched- and compressed-exponential relaxation in liquids and glasses from the dynamics of interacting local relaxation events, the same equation has subsequently appeared in broader contexts, including polymer relaxation and nonlinear models of global population dynamics. This review retraces the conceptual development of the equation, with particular emphasis on its physical origin in Kostya Trachenko's feed-forward interaction mechanism, its mathematical structure, and its possible generalizations. We also include personal recollections of the work with Kostya Trachenko at Queen Mary University of London in August 2019, during which the equation emerged in essentially its present form. After reviewing applications to stress relaxation, glassy materials, polymer relaxation and population dynamics, we discuss future directions including time-dependent feedback parameters, coupled order parameters, heterogeneous and spatially resolved formulations, flux terms, network versions and stochastic extensions. The central theme of the review is that the Trachenko-Zaccone equation should be viewed not only as a model of glassy relaxation, but as a general nonlinear feedback equation with potential applications across complex systems.

AI.tldr: This is a review of the Trachenko-Zaccone equation, a nonlinear dynamical framework for non-Debye relaxation in disordered condensed matter, tracing its conceptual development, mathematical structure, physical origins, applications (stress relaxation, glasses, polymers, population dynamics), and future generalizations.
AI.motivation: To consolidate and retrace the conceptual development of the Trachenko-Zaccone equation, emphasizing its physical origin (Trachenko's feed-forward interaction mechanism), and to reposition it from a glassy-relaxation model to a general nonlinear feedback equation applicable across complex systems.
AI.method: The paper is a review that: (1) reconstructs the derivation of the equation from interacting local relaxation events, (2) details its mathematical structure and possible generalizations, (3) recounts the historical origin at Queen Mary University of London in August 2019, (4) surveys applications across stress relaxation, glassy materials, polymer relaxation, and population dynamics, and (5) outlines future directions including time-dependent feedback parameters, coupled order parameters, heterogeneous/spatially-resolved formulations, flux terms, network versions, and stochastic extensions.
AI.result: The review successfully traces the equation's evolution from its origins in liquids and glasses to broader fields, catalogues its diverse applications, and identifies concrete future research directions, thereby establishing the equation as a general nonlinear feedback framework rather than solely a model of glassy relaxation.
AI.conclusion: The Trachenko-Zaccone equation should be viewed as a general nonlinear feedback equation with broad applicability across complex systems, with several promising extensions (time-dependent feedback, coupled order parameters, heterogeneity, stochasticity) remaining to be explored.

title: A differentiable photon-by-photon likelihood for continuous free-energy landscapes and diffusion coefficients from single-molecule FRET
summary: Single-molecule FRET probes the conformational dynamics of biomolecules by measuring the distance between two dyes. The experiment produces a stream of coloured photons, which is only an indirect readout of these dynamics. Recovering the free-energy landscape and diffusion coefficient from such a photon stream is a difficult inverse problem. Existing approaches assume a small number of discrete states, bin the photons, or are computationally expensive. Here we derive an exact likelihood for the recorded photon stream under a model in which the dye distance diffuses on a continuous free-energy landscape. It uses the raw inter-photon times and colours at full time resolution, and analytically integrates out all hidden trajectories. The likelihood is differentiable, so automatic differentiation returns exact gradients with respect to all model parameters. This lets us jointly infer the free-energy landscape, the diffusion coefficient, and the photophysical parameters by gradient-based optimization. On simulated data, we recover free-energy landscapes, including ones with a short-lived intermediate, together with the diffusion coefficients. Uncertainties follow from the curvature of the likelihood, computed directly from the same gradients. The framework also guides experimental design. Before any data are recorded, we can evaluate how much a given acquisition setting reduces the resulting uncertainty. Evaluation on the GPU is fast, and independent traces are processed in parallel, so a single fit converges in minutes and scales to large datasets. The likelihood extends photon-by-photon analysis to continuous free-energy landscapes and diffusion coefficients, putting fast quantitative inference with uncertainties within reach of the smFRET community.

AI.tldr: This paper derives an exact, differentiable likelihood for single-molecule FRET photon streams under a continuous free-energy landscape diffusion model, enabling joint inference of free-energy landscapes, diffusion coefficients, and photophysical parameters via gradient-based optimization with automatic differentiation, GPU acceleration, and uncertainty quantification from likelihood curvature.
AI.motivation: Recovering free-energy landscapes and diffusion coefficients from smFRET photon streams is a difficult inverse problem. Existing approaches rely on discrete-state assumptions, photon binning, or computationally expensive methods, limiting accuracy and scalability.
AI.method: An exact likelihood is derived for raw inter-photon times and colors at full time resolution under a model where the dye distance diffuses on a continuous free-energy landscape. All hidden trajectories are integrated out analytically, and the likelihood is differentiable such that automatic differentiation yields exact gradients, enabling gradient-based joint inference of all model parameters. Uncertainty is obtained from the likelihood curvature, and experimental design is guided by predicting parameter uncertainty before data collection.
AI.result: On simulated data, the method recovers free-energy landscapes (including those with short-lived intermediates) and diffusion coefficients. GPU evaluation is fast, independent traces are processed in parallel, and a single fit converges in minutes while scaling to large datasets. The approach also evaluates acquisition settings for experimental design before any data are recorded.
AI.conclusion: The framework extends photon-by-photon analysis to continuous free-energy landscapes and diffusion coefficients, providing fast quantitative inference with uncertainties that is directly accessible to the smFRET community.

title: Emergent Vibronic Spectral Hierarchy in a Kagome Flat-Band Insulator
summary: Electron-phonon coupling is usually understood in terms of electronic quasiparticles interacting with dispersive lattice vibrations. Much less is known about the complementary limit in which the relevant phonon mode is itself localized or weakly dispersive. Here we investigate this regime in the kagome compound Rb$_{2}$Ni$_{3}$S$_{4}$, which undergoes an unconventional insulating transition near $T^{*} \approx$ 260-280~K. Combining polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy with temperature-dependent x-ray diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, and electrical, thermal, and magnetic measurements, we show that the transition involves electronic localization without a conventional structural or magnetic order parameter. Raman spectra reveal a giant Franck-Condon progression associated with a nearly dispersionless 333.7~cm$^{-1}$ phonon, decorated by an equally spaced comb-like fine structure with a characteristic spacing of 40.6~cm$^{-1}$. The comb spacing is insensitive to magnetic field, whereas its spectral weight is strongly field tunable. Rather than treating either hierarchy alone as pure phonon effect, we interpret their nested coexistence as evidence for a strongly coupled electron-vibrational manifold involving a localized lattice coordinate. These results identify dispersionless phonons as an active route to vibronic correlations in solids and suggest that such electron-vibrational self-trapping is closely associated with the insulating phase of Rb$_{2}$Ni$_{3}$S$_{4}$.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the kagome compound Rb₂Ni₃S₄, which undergoes an unconventional insulating transition near T* ≈ 260-280 K. Using multiple characterization techniques, the authors discover a giant Franck-Condon progression associated with a nearly dispersionless 333.7 cm⁻¹ phonon, decorated by a comb-like fine structure with 40.6 cm⁻¹ spacing. They interpret this nested structure as evidence for strongly coupled electron-vibrational manifold involving a localized lattice coordinate, identifying dispersionless phonons as an active route to vibronic correlations in solids.
AI.motivation: While electron-phonon coupling is typically understood in terms of electronic quasiparticles interacting with dispersive lattice vibrations, much less is known about the complementary limit where the phonon mode is itself localized or weakly dispersive. The authors aim to investigate this unexplored regime.
AI.method: Combining polarization-resolved Raman spectroscopy with temperature-dependent x-ray diffraction, scanning tunneling microscopy, and electrical, thermal, and magnetic measurements, the authors characterize the unconventional insulating transition in Rb₂Ni₃S₄ (T* ≈ 260-280 K).
AI.result: The transition involves electronic localization without a conventional structural or magnetic order parameter. Raman spectra reveal a giant Franck-Condon progression from a nearly dispersionless 333.7 cm⁻¹ phonon, decorated by an equally spaced comb-like fine structure (40.6 cm⁻¹ spacing). The comb spacing is magnetic-field insensitive but its spectral weight is strongly field tunable. The nested coexistence is interpreted as evidence for a strongly coupled electron-vibrational manifold involving a localized lattice coordinate.
AI.conclusion: Dispersionless (localized) phonons can serve as an active route to vibronic correlations in solids, and electron-vibrational self-trapping appears closely associated with the insulating phase of Rb₂Ni₃S₄.

title: Machine Learning Guided Discovery of Corundum High Entropy Oxides
summary: Early thinking in the field of high entropy oxides (HEOs) emphasized their likely abundance, with combinatorial arguments hinting at a myriad of new materials. The experimental reality has proven more challenging: the stability of HEOs cannot be straightforwardly predicted based on ionic radii, lattice geometry, and charge-balancing considerations alone. In this work, we employ machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) to predict the synthesizability of HEOs of the form $A_2$O$_3$ derived from a selection of trivalent cations. From nearly 500 possible compositions, we identify 16 promising candidates for experimental validation with solid-state and combustion synthesis. We discover three new HEOs in the corundum structure, including (Al,Cr,Fe,Rh,Sc)$_2$O$_3$, and one novel cation-ordered phase, (Al,Fe,Ga,Sc)$_2$O$_3$. By far the most common synthesis outcome was a mixture of competing phases, sometimes involving redox reactions. Our results also reveal profound synthesis method dependence for the final product, where qualitatively equivalent outcomes between the two synthesis methods were only observed for 3 of the 16 tested compositions. We conclude that the occurrence rate of HEOs is far rarer than initially believed and that machine learning approaches can effectively guide us to the "needle in the haystack".

AI.tldr: Machine learning interatomic potentials predict synthesizable A₂O₃ high entropy oxides from ~500 candidates, identifying 16 for experimental validation, yielding 3 new corundum HEOs and 1 cation-ordered phase.
AI.motivation: Early combinatorial arguments suggested high entropy oxides should be abundant, but experimental reality shows their stability cannot be predicted from simple ionic radii, lattice geometry, and charge-balancing considerations alone, motivating the need for better predictive tools.
AI.method: Employed machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) to predict synthesizability of A₂O₃ HEOs from trivalent cations, screening ~500 compositions, then validating top candidates via solid-state and combustion synthesis.
AI.result: Identified 16 promising candidates, discovering 3 new corundum-structure HEOs including (Al,Cr,Fe,Rh,Sc)₂O₃ and one cation-ordered phase (Al,Fe,Ga,Sc)₂O₃. Most compositions yielded competing phase mixtures, and synthesis method dependence was profound—only 3 of 16 compositions gave qualitatively equivalent outcomes across the two synthesis methods.
AI.conclusion: HEOs are far rarer than initially believed, and machine learning approaches can effectively guide discovery of new HEOs within vast compositional spaces.

title: Maxwell's Demon in Markov Chain Monte Carlo: Cooling Information Flow and Entropy Balance
summary: Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms can be viewed as feedback devices that compare a proposed move with the target distribution and then accept or reject it. In this paper the Maxwell demon is identified with the acceptance module: it measures a proposed edge, stores the outcome in the accept/reject bit, and uses that bit to shape the probability current. The decision bit carries a genuine Shannon mutual information about the proposal, whereas only its directional part is converted into a cooling information flow. The relative-entropy relaxation rate obeys $v(t)=\dot{\mathcal I}_{\rm cool}(t)+\dot S(t)$, which separates useful cooling from housekeeping circulation in nonreversible chains.

AI.tldr: This paper interprets Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms as feedback devices operated by a Maxwell demon, where the acceptance/rejection decision acts as the demon's measurement and memory. It shows that the decision bit carries genuine Shannon mutual information about the proposal, but only its directional part converts into a cooling information flow. The authors derive a relative-entropy relaxation rate equation v(t)=İ_cool(t)+Ṡ(t) that separates useful cooling from housekeeping circulation in nonreversible Markov chains.
AI.motivation: To provide a thermodynamically and information-theoretically grounded interpretation of MCMC algorithms by identifying the acceptance module as a Maxwell demon, thereby clarifying how information is processed and converted into useful sampling work versus dissipative circulation.
AI.method: The paper frames MCMC as a feedback control system where the accept/reject bit serves as the demon's memory. It analyzes the information flow between the proposal and the decision bit using Shannon mutual information, distinguishes directional information from total information, and derives a decomposition of the relative-entropy relaxation rate into a cooling information flow and a housekeeping entropy-production term.
AI.result: The decision bit stores genuine Shannon mutual information about the proposal, yet only its directional component contributes to cooling. The derived decomposition v(t)=İ_cool(t)+Ṡ(t) shows that in nonreversible chains, the relative-entropy relaxation rate separates into useful cooling flow and housekeeping circulation entropy production.
AI.conclusion: The Maxwell-demon feedback perspective provides a clean information-theoretic separation of the useful (cooling) and wasteful (housekeeping) components of the relaxation process in nonreversible MCMC, linking the accept/reject decision to genuine information processing and thermodynamic bookkeeping.

title: Intracavity Photon Statistics from Correlated Molecular Electronic Structure
summary: Quantum optics characterizes light through photon correlations, but ab initio cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED) has only calculated raw field moments at present. In this study, intracavity photon statistics of cavity-coupled molecules are computed from QED coupled-cluster (QED-CCSD-22) densities and validated against exact diagonalization of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian. A change of coordinate origin or dipole convention displaces the ground state coherently, so second-order and higher cumulants of the cavity field are well defined even for molecular ions. The photon subsystem of QED Hartree-Fock is exactly coherent, so the invariant statistics measure electron-photon correlation. The field fluctuations are super-Poissonian, and their degree of second-order coherence is set by the cavity frequency rather than by the coupling strength, falling from 18.5 to 4.9 for H2 as the cavity is detuned from 5 to 20 eV. A parity selection rule makes the sign of the third cumulant a probe of the orientation of the molecular charge asymmetry along the cavity polarization.

AI.tldr: This paper computes intracavity photon statistics of cavity-coupled molecules using QED coupled-cluster (QED-CCSD-22) densities, validated against exact diagonalization of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian. It shows that cumulants beyond second order are well-defined and invariant to coordinate/dipole choices, photon subsystem at QED Hartree-Fock is exactly coherent, field fluctuations are super-Poissonian with second-order coherence set by cavity frequency (18.5 to 4.9 for H2 from 5 to 20 eV), and a parity selection rule makes the third cumulant a probe of molecular charge asymmetry orientation.
AI.motivation: Quantum optics characterizes light via photon correlations, but ab initio cavity QED has previously only computed raw field moments. The authors aim to bridge this gap by computing genuine photon statistics (cumulants, coherence functions) from QED coupled-cluster densities, addressing issues of gauge/dipole convention in defining cavity field cumulants.
AI.method: The authors use QED coupled-cluster (QED-CCSD-22) to compute intracavity photon statistics from reduced photon densities, validated against exact diagonalization of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian. They define invariant second-order and higher cumulants that are well-defined despite coherent displacement of the ground state under coordinate origin or dipole convention changes. They derive photon statistics (degree of second-order coherence, third-order cumulants) and analyze the coherent nature of QED Hartree-Fock photon subsystems.
AI.result: The photon subsystem at QED Hartree-Fock level is exactly coherent, so invariant statistics measure electron-photon correlation. Field fluctuations are super-Poissonian, with degree of second-order coherence set by cavity frequency rather than coupling strength—falling from 18.5 to 4.9 for H2 as the cavity detunes from 5 to 20 eV. A parity selection rule makes the sign of the third cumulant a probe of the orientation of molecular charge asymmetry along the cavity polarization.
AI.conclusion: Intracavity photon statistics can be reliably computed from QED coupled-cluster densities, providing invariant measures of electron-photon correlation beyond raw field moments. The field statistics are governed by cavity frequency, and the third cumulant offers a directional probe of molecular charge asymmetry orientation relative to the cavity polarization.

title: Two distinct gap structures in the mid-infrared optical conductivity of the Hubbard model
summary: Mid-infrared (MIR) optical conductivities in cuprate superconductors show universal features. In this study, we demonstrate that these originate from two distinct gaps: the pseudogap mediated by antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations and the Mott-Hubbard gap. The MIR spectra from these two gaps show a characteristic and distinct shape and doping dependence, and can thus be distinguished. Specifically, the Mott-Hubbard correlations, while rendering a peak in the visible spectrum for small dopings, yield a broad optical response starting in the MIR when a ``waterfall'' develops in the one-particle spectrum at larger dopings. The numerically and analytically determined doping-dependence of both gaps consistently reproduce experiments, and provide a unified microscopic understanding of the cuprate MIR optical conductivity.

AI.tldr: The paper explains universal mid-infrared optical conductivity features in cuprate superconductors as originating from two distinct gaps: the pseudogap mediated by antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations and the Mott-Hubbard gap, each exhibiting characteristic and distinguishable shapes and doping dependencies that reproduce experimental observations.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified microscopic understanding of the universal MIR optical conductivity features observed in cuprate superconductors, which had previously lacked a consistent theoretical explanation.
AI.method: Numerical and analytical analysis of the doping dependence of both the pseudogap (mediated by antiferromagnetic spin fluctuations) and the Mott-Hubbard gap, and their respective contributions to the MIR optical conductivity spectra.
AI.result: The two gaps produce characteristically distinct MIR spectral shapes and doping dependences. Mott-Hubbard correlations produce a visible-region peak at small dopings and a broad MIR response once a "waterfall" appears in the one-particle spectrum at larger dopings. Both gaps' doping dependences consistently match experiments.
AI.conclusion: The universal MIR optical conductivity features in cuprates arise from the combined, distinguishable contributions of the pseudogap and the Mott-Hubbard gap, offering a unified microscopic description consistent with experimental data.

title: Long-lived Laughlin pairs in a depleted quantum Hall edge channel
summary: On-demand sources and mesoscopic beam splitters allow individual ballistic electrons to collide in depleted quantum Hall edge channels, where their unscreened Coulomb interaction acts as a strong, controllable nonlinearity. Theory suggests a more striking possibility: in a strong magnetic field, the repulsion can drive quantized relative circulation, allowing two electrons to propagate together as a positive-energy Laughlin pair. The relevance of such pairs to experiment depends on quantitative lifetimes in realistic guiding potentials and on whether the proposed collision pathway to pair formation survives full two-dimensional dynamics. We develop a microscopic theory of quasibound Laughlin pairs using the physical two-electron Hamiltonian. For a general local electric-field gradient, we determine the dissociation threshold, number of quasibound states, and decay rates. Complex scaling and analytic tunneling theory show that lifetimes grow exponentially with pair energy above threshold. Applied to reported GaAs parameters, the theory indicates that existing devices may already support the lowest spin-polarized pair, with a leading lifetime estimate about three orders of magnitude longer than typical propagation times. We simulate a collision with the full finite-field Hamiltonian, demonstrating both a framework for nonlinear two-electron quantum dynamics and the creation of a Laughlin pair in a representative two-electron collision. We use Husimi distributions and their zeros to visualize both quasibound resonances and transient collision states in phase space. These results place the preparation, propagation, and detection of repulsively paired electrons within reach of existing single-electron circuit technology. They identify kinematic stabilization under constrained one-dimensional propagation as a pairing mechanism that may extend to anyonic quantum Hall edge excitations.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory of quasibound Laughlin pairs in quantum Hall edge channels, showing that repulsively interacting ballistic electrons can form positive-energy bound pairs with exponentially long lifetimes above the dissociation threshold. Applied to GaAs parameters, lifetimes are ~1000x longer than typical propagation times, suggesting existing single-electron circuits can create, propagate, and detect these pairs. Full two-dimensional collision simulations demonstrate pair formation, and the mechanism may extend to anyonic excitations.
AI.motivation: Theory predicted that two electrons in a strong magnetic field with unscreened Coulomb repulsion could form positive-energy Laughlin pairs with quantized relative circulation. However, the practical relevance of these pairs was uncertain—it was unknown whether they would have sufficiently long lifetimes in realistic guiding potentials and whether the collision pathway to pair formation survives full two-dimensional dynamics. This work addresses both questions quantitatively.
AI.method: The authors develop a microscopic theory of quasibound Laughlin pairs using the physical two-electron Hamiltonian. They use complex scaling and analytic tunneling theory to determine dissociation thresholds, number of quasibound states, and decay rates as functions of the local electric-field gradient. They also perform full finite-field Hamiltonian simulations of two-electron collisions to test pair formation, visualizing resonances and transient states via Husimi distributions and their zeros in phase space.
AI.result: Lifetimes grow exponentially with pair energy above threshold. Applied to reported GaAs parameters, the theory indicates existing devices may already support the lowest spin-polarized pair, with a leading lifetime estimate about three orders of magnitude longer than typical propagation times. Collision simulations with the full finite-field Hamiltonian demonstrate the creation of a Laughlin pair in a representative two-electron collision.
AI.conclusion: The preparation, propagation, and detection of repulsively paired electrons are within reach of existing single-electron circuit technology. The kinematic stabilization under constrained one-dimensional propagation identified here may serve as a general pairing mechanism extending to anyonic quantum Hall edge excitations.

title: Orbital-Selective Spin Splitting in the Altermagnetic Ti$_2$XX' Monolayers
summary: Altermagnets have attracted intensive attention recently, owing to their unique combination of zero net magnetic moment of antiferromagnets and momentum space spin-splitting of ferromagnets. Herein, we systematically explore monolayer altermagnetic Ti$_2$XX' (X/X' = F, Cl, Br, I) materials for novel electronic properties. Especifically, spin-splitting exists in the valence bands of all studied materials, whereas several compositions exhibit nearly spin-degenerate conduction bands near the Fermi level, which is markedly different from conventional altermagnets. This phenomenon can be attributed to the bond-angle-sensitive super-exchange occurring in the $d_{xz}$ or $d_{yz}$ orbitals, while the super-exchange of the $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbital is not sensitive to the Ti-X-Ti bond angle. Motivated by this intriguing phenomenon, Fermi level modulation via doping or heterostructure construction enables the transition between two electronic states, endowing these materials great application potential in information storage devices.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically explores monolayer altermagnetic Ti2XX' (X/X' = F, Cl, Br, I) materials, revealing spin-splitting in valence bands across all compositions but nearly spin-degenerate conduction bands in some cases—a feature distinct from conventional altermagnets. This arises from bond-angle-sensitive super-exchange in d_xz/d_yz orbitals versus insensitive super-exchange in d_x²-y² orbitals. Fermi level tuning via doping or heterostructures enables switching between electronic states, promising for information storage devices.
AI.motivation: Altermagnets combine the zero net magnetization of antiferromagnets with the momentum-space spin-splitting of ferromagnets, making them highly interesting. The authors aim to explore novel monolayer altermagnetic Ti2XX' materials to uncover unique electronic properties and expand the altermagnet materials family.
AI.method: The authors systematically investigate monolayer altermagnetic Ti2XX' (X/X' = F, Cl, Br, I) compounds via first-principles calculations, analyzing spin-splitting in band structures and correlating electronic features with orbital-specific super-exchange mechanisms sensitive to Ti-X-Ti bond angles.
AI.result: All studied Ti2XX' monolayers exhibit spin-splitting in valence bands, but several compositions show nearly spin-degenerate conduction bands near the Fermi level—atypical for altermagnets. This asymmetry is explained by bond-angle-sensitive super-exchange in d_xz/d_yz orbitals, while d_x²-y² orbital super-exchange is bond-angle insensitive. Doping or heterostructure engineering can modulate the Fermi level to switch between two electronic states.
AI.conclusion: Monolayer Ti2XX' altermagnets exhibit a distinctive valence-band spin-splitting/conduction-band spin-degeneracy dichotomy driven by orbital-dependent super-exchange behavior. Fermi-level modulation via doping or heterostructures enables electronic state transitions, positioning these materials as strong candidates for information storage applications.

title: Neural quantum states in condensed matter: advances, best practices, and prospects
summary: Neural quantum states provide flexible variational representations of quantum many-body wave functions by combining neural-network parametrizations with Monte Carlo sampling. In this perspective, we review recent advances in their application to condensed-matter systems, focusing on frustrated quantum magnets, interacting lattice fermions, and non-equilibrium dynamics. We discuss the architectures, symmetry constraints, optimization methods, and sampling strategies underlying state-of-the-art calculations, and summarize practical guidelines for reliable simulations. We also examine the principal remaining challenges, including learning non-trivial sign and phase structures, controlling variational bias, enforcing physical symmetries, scaling optimization to large networks, and achieving stable real-time evolution. Finally, we outline promising directions in which neural quantum states may extend the reach of classical simulations of strongly correlated quantum matter.

AI.tldr: This perspective reviews recent advances in neural quantum states (NQS) applied to condensed-matter systems, covering architectures, symmetry constraints, optimization methods, and sampling strategies for frustrated magnets, interacting fermions, and non-equilibrium dynamics. It outlines remaining challenges including sign structure learning, variational bias control, symmetry enforcement, large-scale optimization, and stable real-time evolution, while suggesting promising future directions.
AI.motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the current state of neural quantum states and guide practitioners by summarizing state-of-the-art techniques, practical guidelines, and open challenges in applying these methods to strongly correlated quantum matter.
AI.method: The paper is a perspective/review that synthesizes recent developments in neural quantum states, covering: (1) neural-network architectures for wave function parametrization, (2) symmetry constraints for physical consistency, (3) optimization methods for variational training, and (4) Monte Carlo sampling strategies. It examines applications to frustrated quantum magnets, interacting lattice fermions, and non-equilibrium dynamics.
AI.result: A systematic overview of practical guidelines for reliable NQS simulations is provided, along with a clear identification of the principal remaining challenges: learning non-trivial sign and phase structures, controlling variational bias, enforcing physical symmetries, scaling optimization to large networks, and achieving stable real-time evolution.
AI.conclusion: Neural quantum states hold significant promise for extending the reach of classical simulations of strongly correlated quantum matter, with several well-defined future directions identified to overcome current limitations.

title: Machine-Learned NMR Shieldings in Molecular Solids with Built-In Hybrid-Functional Molecular Corrections
summary: Fast and accurate chemical shielding estimators are essential for shielding-driven Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) crystallography. Machine-learning models for shielding predictions have matured significantly and today are primarily limited by the electronic structure reference data they are trained on. Here, we introduce ShiftML4, a shielding-tensor model trained directly on monomer-corrected calculations that approximate PBE0, rather than the PBE reference targeted by earlier ShiftML models. ShiftML4 is trained on a diverse set of structures containing 12 of the most common NMR nuclei in molecular organic solids. On experimental benchmark sets, the 13C isotropic RMSE against experiment is 1.67 ppm, compared with 2.34 ppm for GIPAW-PBE on the same geometries. ShiftML4 gives a similar 1H prediction RMSE to ShiftML3 (0.5 ppm) and improves the 15N RMSE from 7.24 to 6.08 ppm. The model also reduces errors in the shielding-tensor anisotropy, with an RMSE of 4.63 ppm on 13C CSA principal components against 5.85 ppm for GIPAW. The improvements in prediction accuracy are retained on better geometries. Basing shift predictions on structures relaxed with PET-MOLS, a recent machine-learned interatomic potential that reaches approximate hybrid-DFT geometries in seconds, lowers the ShiftML4 errors further to 0.48 ppm (1H), 1.49 ppm (13C) and 3.66 ppm (15N).

AI.tldr: ShiftML4 is a machine-learning shielding-tensor model trained on monomer-corrected PBE0-approximate calculations, covering 12 common NMR nuclei in molecular organic solids. It outperforms earlier ShiftML models and GIPAW-PBE on experimental benchmarks, achieving 13C RMSE of 1.67 ppm, 1H RMSE of 0.5 ppm, and 15N RMSE of 6.08 ppm, with further improvements when combined with hybrid-DFT-quality geometries from PET-MOLS.
AI.motivation: Chemical shielding prediction is critical for NMR crystallography, and machine-learning models are now limited by the quality of the electronic structure reference data they are trained on. Since earlier ShiftML models targeted PBE-level reference data, there is a need for a model trained on higher-accuracy (approximate PBE0) reference data to improve prediction fidelity.
AI.method: ShiftML4 is a shielding-tensor machine-learning model trained on monomer-corrected calculations approximating PBE0 level of theory, covering structures with 12 common NMR nuclei in molecular organic solids. The model is evaluated on experimental benchmarks and combined with PET-MOLS-relaxed geometries (a machine-learned interatomic potential providing approximate hybrid-DFT structures) to assess performance with improved structures.
AI.result: ShiftML4 achieves 13C isotropic RMSE of 1.67 ppm (vs 2.34 ppm for GIPAW-PBE), 1H RMSE of 0.5 ppm (comparable to ShiftML3), and improves 15N RMSE from 7.24 to 6.08 ppm. It also reduces shielding-tensor anisotropy errors, with 13C CSA principal component RMSE of 4.63 ppm vs 5.85 ppm for GIPAW. Using PET-MOLS-relaxed geometries further lowers errors to 0.48 ppm (1H), 1.49 ppm (13C), and 3.66 ppm (15N).
AI.conclusion: Training on higher-level monomer-corrected PBE0-approximate reference data substantially improves shielding prediction accuracy across multiple nuclei and tensor components. Combining ShiftML4 with machine-learned high-quality geometries (PET-MOLS) yields the best performance, demonstrating the value of both improved reference data and improved structural models for NMR crystallography.

title: Dissipation driven boundary localization in higher order topological insulators
summary: We study dissipation driven boundary localization in a Bernevig Hughes Zhang type second order topological insulator by introducing inhomogeneous, spin dependent boundary dissipation. After projection onto the edge subspace, the dominant component of the boundary dissipation lies in the same Pauli channel as the kinetic term. This channel gives both counter-propagating edge modes the same real transfer exponent. The two modes therefore accumulate at the same dissipative domain wall. For the corner states, the dissipative envelope competes with Jackiw Rebbi localization. Increasing dissipation moves their weight from the geometric corners to the dissipative domain wall. title: Magnetic-Field Selection of Magnetic Order in Altermagnets and Noncollinear Antiferromagnets
summary: Conventional field selection of magnetic order relies on the Zeeman coupling, which, however, vanishes in magnets without net magnetization, a rapidly growing class including altermagnets (AMs), noncollinear antiferromagnets (nc-AFMs), and PT-symmetric antiferromagnets (PT-AFMs). Here we show that the quantity that fundamentally couples a magnet to a uniform magnetic field is not the magnetization, but the binary order parameter eta that labels the two time-reversal-related minima of the Landau free energy. We develop a Landau theory of order selection based on eta under the constraints of magnetic point-group (MPG) symmetry, in which eta couples to odd-degree polynomials in the magnetic field. Within this framework, the linear term is the ferromagnetic Zeeman coupling, while higher-order couplings with leading degree n = 3, 5, 7, and 9 naturally appear in AMs and nc-AFMs. In contrast, combined PT symmetry forbids any such coupling. Consequently, it is the order-(n-1) magnetic susceptibility, rather than the net magnetization, that serves as the primary experimental observable for identifying the magnetic order of AMs and nc-AFMs. For all 122 MPGs, we classify the leading coupling degree and the corresponding polynomial forms. We demonstrate our framework in two representative materials: the AM MnF2 and the nc-AFM MnTe2. We further construct a symmetry-allowed spin model for an AM system to reveal the microscopic origin of the higher-order coupling and establish the coupling coefficient explicitly in terms of the spin-model parameters. Our work unifies the description of magnetic-order selection across magnets with and without net magnetization, offers a microscopic origin for this counterintuitive physics, and provides fingerprints for distinguishing intrinsic field selection from extrinsic switching.

title: Machine learning predictions of the Hessian matrix for peptides chains and small proteins
summary: Molecular Hessians have a key role in describing molecular vibrations, trajectories and optimization paths. An explicit calculation of them through standard quantum mechanical methods can be computationally expensive for medium-large systems, and in many applications not even needed. Machine learning methods can be a shortcut to tackle efficiently the computational difficulties. This paper will present a ML model able to predict the Hessian matrix of biological system made of thousands of atoms. The method, based on learning the Hessian in internal coordinates is intrinsically invariant to molecular rotations and translations, and has a very good scaling with the systems' size. The training was performed on a dataset of simple aminoacids, as they constitute the building blocks of larger proteins. From the predicted Hessian matrix it is possible to calculate thermochemical properties within the harmonic approximations, among them enthalpies, entropies, Gibbs' free energies, and zero point vibrational energies.

The method learns Hessians in internal coordinates, making it invariant to molecular rotations and translations, and scales well with system size. Trained on simple aminoacids, it enables calculation of thermochemical properties (enthalpies, entropies, Gibbs free energies, and zero-point vibrational energies) within the harmonic approximation.

AI.method: The authors propose a machine learning model that predicts the Hessian matrix of biological systems. The Hessian is learned in internal coordinates, which intrinsically guarantees invariance to molecular rotations and translations. The model exhibits favorable scaling with system size and is trained on a dataset of simple aminoacids, which are the building blocks of larger proteins.

title: Ultralow-Field Triplon Condensation in a Spin-Ladder Magnet

summary: We realise the first ultralow-field Bose-Einstein condensation of triplons in a spin-ladder magnet, uncovering a quantum critical point at only $μ_0 H_{c1}=0.17$ T in Henmilite ($\mathrm{Ca_2Cu(OH)_4[B(OH)_4]_2}$). Unlike dimer magnets, a ladder retains extended one-dimensional correlations in its gapped parent state, making this limit strongly fluctuation dominated. Thermodynamic, magnetoelastic, $μ$SR, and neutron-diffraction measurements overturn the previous assignment of zero-field antiferromagnetic order, establishing a quantum-disordered coupled-ladder parent state with persistent low-energy dynamics. The weak low-temperature anomaly instead marks a gap-controlled crossover from the correlated ladder regime into the activated quantum-disordered state. These measurements further reveal an exceptionally asymmetric ordered dome extending to $μ_0 H_{c2}\simeq 8.2$ T. Quantum Monte Carlo simulations for the relevant spin Hamiltonian place Henmilite just on the gapped side of the zero-field ladder-ordering instability, naturally accounting for the strong separation between the exchange and residual-gap scales and the tiny critical field. Our findings extend ultralow-field triplon condensation beyond the dimer paradigm and establish Henmilite as a platform for controlled tuning across quantum criticality in a fluctuation-dominated spin ladder.

title: Interedge backscattering in quantum spin Hall-based NS and SNS junctions
comment: 9+6 pages and 5+7 figures, comments are welcome
summary: We investigate the microscopic conditions that allow for the coupling between opposite quantum spin Hall (QSH) edges in hybrid junctions with superconductors. Using a microscopic Bernevig--Hughes--Zhang model and the Bogoliubov--de Gennes formalism, we model a potential barrier along the NS interface and identify the parameter regimes in which the QSH edges are coupled. In normal--superconductor junctions, such coupling manifests as deviations from the quantized zero-bias Andreev conductance $G=4e^2/h$. These deviations are controlled by the induced gap in the barrier, the barrier geometry, the interface transparency, orbital and Fermi-velocity mismatch, and disorder strength as well as the bias voltage leading to a zero-bias peak. We then analyze the impact of this interedge-coupling mechanism in Josephson junctions at equilibrium and show that it hybridizes the edge-resolved Andreev branches, opens gaps at the time-reversal-invariant phase differences $\varphi=0$ and $\varphi=π$, and modifies the superconducting quantum interference pattern. In a reflection-symmetric geometry, the relative sizes of the two gap openings provide complementary information about the interedge dynamical phase, which also determines the parity of the suppressed lobes in the magnetic interference pattern. This investigation sheds light on the microscopic details that control the coupling of helical edge states in actual devices and the resulting consequences for superconducting hybrid systems.

title: Prediction of a layer nonlinear Hall effect in bilayer nonmagnetic or antiferromagnetic systems
summary: Nonlinear Hall effects provide a powerful probe of quantum geometry in solids and enable rectification phenomena beyond the constraints of linear response. In this Letter, we predict a \emph{layer nonlinear Hall effect} (LNHE) in stacked bilayer systems composed of nonmagnetic or antiferromagnetic materials with a vanishing linear Hall conductivity. In such systems, the second- or third-order nonlinear Hall responses are intrinsically layer odd: the contributions from the two constituent layers have equal magnitude but opposite sign, resulting in exact cancellation under layer-exchange symmetry. An out-of-plane electric field $E_z$ can break this symmetry, thereby unveiling the hidden response and converting it into a switchable macroscopic nonlinear Hall signal. Using a minimal $k\!\cdot\!p$ model, we demonstrate that the LNHE can originate from the Berry curvature dipole mechanism. A systematic symmetry analysis of all 80 layer groups further yields a complete classification of the symmetry constraints and stacking configurations that allow for this type of LNHE. Beyond this mechanism, additional symmetry analysis reveals that LNHE may also arise from quantum metric dipole or inversed mass dipole. Remarkably, even in cases where second-order nonlinear Hall responses are symmetry forbidden, a third-order LNHE can still survive in certain stacked bilayer configurations. First-principles calculations on representative bilayers---nonmagnetic 1T$'$-WTe$_2$ and 1T$'$-ReS$_2$---explicitly demonstrate electrically reversible second-order LNHE, in full agreement with our symmetry-based predictions. Overall, our results establish LNHE as a universal phenomenon in a wide range of layered quantum materials and provide a robust route toward electrically tunable nonlinear transport.

title: Optical conductivity signature of Van Hove singularity in altermagnetic topological systems
summary: We investigate the topological phases, joint density of states (JDOS), optical conductivities, and magneto-optical responses of a two-dimensional $d$-wave altermagnet with spin-orbit coupling and Zeeman splitting. The system hosts Dirac gaps at the high-symmetry points $Γ$, $\textrm{M}$, $\textrm{X}$, and $\textrm{Y}$. We show that the JDOS exhibits kinks at the corresponding Dirac gap frequencies and pronounced peaks at Van Hove singularities, whose positions can be tuned by the altermagnetic order. These features are reflected in the optical conductivities, with complementary signatures in their real and imaginary parts. Particularly, the Van Hove signatures in the transverse optical conductivity disappear in the absence of $d$-wave altermagnetism, revealing an altermagnet-induced optical signature of the Van Hove singularity. Finally, the Faraday and Kerr rotations inherit characteristic features of the optical conductivity. Our results establish optical and magneto-optical spectroscopy as sensitive probes of Dirac gaps and Van Hove singularities in altermagnetic topological systems.

title: First-principles design of main-group dimer defects in ZnO as candidate quantum defects
summary: Zinc oxide (ZnO), a wide-band-gap semiconductor with mature growth techniques, is a promising host for optically active quantum spins. Using hybrid density functional theory (DFT), we systematically investigate double substitutional DA complexes and their defect physics, including electronic structure, thermodynamic stability, and optical properties. The proposed defects exhibit isolated defect states, strong spin localization on the acceptor site, and $C_{3v}$ symmetry. Importantly, the electronic structure of the DA pairs is largely determined by the atomic properties of their constituent atoms. We further examine their optical characteristics, including zero-phonon lines (ZPLs), radiative lifetimes, and nonradiative decay to assess their viability as color centers. Notably, among the dimers, (Si$_{Zn}$-B$_O$)$^+$ and (Ge$_{Zn}$-B$_O$)$^+$ exhibit visible optical transitions with sub-microsecond radiative lifetimes and robust charge states against optical ionization, while (Si$_{Zn}$-C$_O$)$^{2+}$ shows the smallest Huang-Rhys factor, approximately 5.6. Our results propose a new family of main-group donor-acceptor defects in ZnO as promising candidates for optically active spin defects.

title: Quasi-one-dimensional topological band structure and van Hove singularities in monolayer TaIrTe$_4$ from laser $μ$-ARPES
summary: Recent transport experiments reported a quantum spin Hall insulator phase in monolayer 1T-TaIrTe$_4$ gated away from charge neutrality. We find a strongly anisotropic band structure susceptible to density wave instabilities. Our data further reveal a saddle point singularity in the density of states. However, we find that the saddle point lies at a density for which transport experiments found no anomalies. Moreover, the quasiparticle line widths suggest weak electron correlations only. This points to a secondary role of van Hove singularities and electron correlations in the transport phase diagram of monolayer 1T-TaIrTe$_4$.

title: Electric-Field-Induced Second Harmonic Generation at a Reconfigurable LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ Nanojunction
summary: Electrically tunable nonlinear optical responses at the nanoscale remain challenging to achieve because conventional nonlinear materials lack the combination of large susceptibility, nanoscale confinement, and in situ reconfigurability. Here we report electric-field-induced second harmonic (EFISH) generation from a nanoscale tunnel junction defined by conductive atomic force microscope lithography at the LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ interface. A conducting channel written at the interface is interrupted by a nanoscale insulating gap, across which applied DC bias produces local electric fields exceeding $10^7$ V/m. The SHG signal is spatially localized at the junction, exhibits a quadratic bias dependence described by $I(2ω) \propto |χ^{(2)}_\mathrm{0} + χ^{(3)} E_\mathrm{DC}|^2$ with no hysteresis, a modulation depth exceeding 380% at $|V_\mathrm{DC}| = 1$ V, and shows a two-lobed input-polarization pattern aligned with the junction axis, consistent with EFISH from a centrosymmetric host. Calibration against a BBO reference crystal gives $|χ^{(3)}| \approx 1\times10^{-19}$ m$^2$/V$^2$ at 6 K. These results establish cAFM-written oxide nanojunctions as a reconfigurable platform for nanoscale nonlinear optics in which the junction geometry sets the symmetry of the response and the large field-induced $χ^{(2)}$ of SrTiO$_3$ provides the optical nonlinearity. Because the nonlinearity is both generated and read out within the same nanoscale gap, the junction operates simultaneously as a subwavelength source and a near-field detector of optical nonlinearity.

title: Systematic and accurate anharmonic formation free energies of metastable defects via a constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force framework
summary: Computing the formation free energies of metastable defects at finite temperature remains challenging due to anharmonicity, the multiplicity of basins and the frequent occurrence of migration events. Using the previously introduced constrained Bayesian Adaptive Biasing Force method (BABFc), we establish a practical thermodynamic integration framework for computing restricted anharmonic formation free energies associated with individual metastable defect basins. We demonstrate that BABFc can be exploited as a robust, systematic and numerically efficient tool for addressing a long standing bottleneck in atomistic materials science: the finite temperature thermodynamic characterization of metastable defects in complex, highly anharmonic energy landscapes. The proposed workflow requires only a reference local minimum and a confinement strategy and does not rely on defect specific collective variables. It therefore provides a general route to assign well-defined free energies to individual metastable basins, even when these basins are separated by low barriers and embedded in a dense landscape of competing configurations. In this setting, BABFc enables stable, bias corrected free energy estimates with statistical accuracies at the meV/atom level and a very low failure rate, including for systems containing approximately one thousand atoms. We demonstrate this capability through thousands of independent free energy calculations covering hundreds of four-interstitial and four-vacancy configurations in bcc $α$-Fe over a broad temperature range, using both a traditional empirical potential and a data driven force field.

title: An autonomous feedback protocol: responding to temperature and potential changes in energy converters
